title: Tech Turmoil Ruins GDP Party | Investing.com
text:
Follow
This was supposed to be a session to celebrate a 4.1% GDP in the second quarter, the best reading in nearly 4 years and yet more proof of the economy’s strength. Instead, technology ruined the day. But it didn’t ruin the week…at least not for two of the three major indices. The Dow , which got a big shot in the arm recently on some positive trade headlines, had a solid performance with a more than 1.5% advance over the past 5 days. The S&P was up 0.6% in that time. Looking at the NASDAQ, though, you can really see the tough times for tech of late. The index dropped by 1.1% this week as the FANGs had a mixed performance in their quarterly reports. The week had no shortage of big news items. In addition to today’s strong GDP reading, we got a rare piece of good trade news when President Trump and European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker had a seemingly constructive meeting that everybody hopes will avert a trade war. But what was the BIGGEST news over the past 5 days? It was obviously Facebook’s slaughter on Thursday after reporting soft daily active users and missing revenue expectations. The social media giant had its worst single day in its history with a drop of practically 19%, though it managed to keep today’s slip to less than 1%. Therefore, two FANG stocks (Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX ) and FB) really disappointed the market and have some wondering if the love affair with the tech darlings is over. It didn’t help to see other tech stalwarts like Intel (NASDAQ: INTC ) (-8.6%) and Twitter (-20.5%) have challenging results and subsequently plunge. Let’s see if Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) can change the tide next week. As for Friday’s session, the NASDAQ led the way lower (of course) with a 1.46% plunge to 7737.4. The S&P was off 0.66% to 2818.8 and the Dow slipped 0.30% to 25451.1. The portfolios saw a full day of activity. Healthcare Innovators, Insider Trader and Technology Innovators each cashed in double-digit winners. Meanwhile, Surprise Trader, Value Investor, Counterstrike and Momentum Trader each bought. Let’s get right to it: Today's Portfolio Highlights: Surprise Trader: Last quarter HMS Holdings (HMSY) reported a positive surprise of more than 46% and the stock really took off. Dave thinks this provider of cost containment solutions for the healthcare marketplace is poised for another big beat. It has a positive Earnings ESP for the quarter coming before the bell next Friday. The editor added HMSY today with a 12.5% allocation in hopes for another strong reaction from the market. Read the full commentary for more. Value Investor: For the most part, Tracey is not very fond of auto stocks right now due to all the tariff turmoil in the air. However, she does see an exception with the suppliers, as evidenced by today’s addition of BorgWarner (NYSE: BWA ). Along with a “dirt cheap” valuation, this maker of propulsion systems has a “stellar” management team. The company had a solid quarter yesterday, but most importantly it is navigating all the tariff risks so far. Though down 12% year to date on all the uncertainty, earnings are expected to grow 13% this year. Read the editor’s complete commentary for a lot more on this new addition and her outlook for the space. Counterstrike: The market pretty much gave up on iRobot (IRBT) after it guided lower earlier this year, which explains its 40% short position. But they should’ve known that robots never die and neither did this company. The Roomba robot vacuum maker just reported a “fantastic” quarter with an EPS surprise of 117% and a raised guidance. The stock jumped to $90 from a low of about $60. Jeremy thinks the short sellers will fail to save their position and IRBT is set to soar to $119 long term. Therefore, he added the stock on Friday with an 8% allocation. Read the full write-up for more. Healthcare Innovators: Investors really like the quarterly report from Eli Lilly (LLY), especially its decision to spin-off the underperforming Elanco Animal Health segment into a new publicly-traded company. However, analyst price targets haven’t moved much and remain stuck around $95 on average. Kevin felt this was a great time to trim another large-cap pharma name by selling LLY for a more than 20% profit. This was also the portfolio's 6th long-term gain booked this year. Insider Trader: Shares of John Bean (JBT) soared about 25% yesterday after reporting a positive surprise of more than 18% and conducting an upbeat conference call. The best part, though, is that this food processing and air transportation company held onto most of those gains during today’s challenging market. However, Tracey thinks shares could stagnate here as the good news is now baked in, so the editor decided to sell JBT for a 22% return in less than two months. Technology Innovators: We haven’t seen the earnings report for Twilio (TWLO) yet, but Brian Bolan doesn’t want to wait until August 6th. Basically, the glamour stocks have been taking it on the chin this earnings season, which leaves the editor thinking that this provider of cloud communications platforms has more downside right now than upside. It would take a monster beat for it to be rewarded, so Brian wants to sell the name and take the 10.4% profit while he can. Momentum Trader: The entire energy sector has been “red hot” recently, so it’s no wonder that Dave was able to find a breakout stock with solid momentum in the space. Bonanza Creek Energy (BCEI) is a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) that acquires, explores and develops onshore oil and natural gas properties. Shares and earnings estimates are both moving higher as it heads toward the next quarterly report on August 8. The editor added BCEI today with a 12.5% allocation in hopes that this breakout will continue. The full write-up has more on this new pick.
